title: A finitely presented cartesian system of ring maps detects colimit bijectivity at a stage
statement: Let J be a small filtered category, D,E : J → CommRing diagrams in a universe containing the size of J, α : D → E a natural transformation, and cD,cE colimit cocones [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose f : cD.pt → cE.pt is bijective and αⱼ followed by the target coprojection equals the source coprojection followed by f. Suppose every αⱼ is finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and for every arrow r : j → k the square with αⱼ, D(r), E(r), αₖ is a pushout. Then αⱼ is bijective for some j.

source.place: Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat), proof of (3), comparison maps Ψ; Tags 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation) and 05N9 (lemma-colimit-fp-algebras) (2), (3). Sources checked online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02JO and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05N9.

proof.text: Choose i and restrict to Under i, whose forgetful functor is final. Whisker both colimit cocones. Use the natural structure maps D(i) → D(j) to treat the restricted source diagram as D(i)-algebras. Factor E(i) → cE.pt → cD.pt, the restriction of the inverse of f, through D(k), using finite presentation of αᵢ. The factorization a satisfies αᵢ ≫ a = D(k.hom).

The maps a ≫ αₖ and E(k.hom) agree after passage to cE. Apply the exact Mathlib eventual-equality lemma RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_comp_map_eq_of_isColimit to these D(i)-algebra maps from E(i), using the finite type consequence of finite presentation of αᵢ. Obtain l and arrows r,s in Under i. Set b = a ≫ D(r.right). Naturality and the two Under equations give αᵢ ≫ b = D(l.hom) and b ≫ αₗ = E(l.hom).

source.place: RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_comp_map_eq_of_isColimit, applied over D(i) to E(i) and the target diagram restricted to Under i.

proof.text: Use the pushout square for i → l to define inv : E(l) → D(l) from b and the identity of D(l). The source-leg identity gives αₗ ≫ inv = id. For inv ≫ αₗ = id, use pushout hom-ext: on E(i) this is b ≫ αₗ = E(l.hom), and on D(l) it is the first identity. Applying these identities to elements gives injectivity and surjectivity.

proof_origin.place: Construction made explicit from the cited Stacks proof; bijectivity argument formalized directly from Mathlib.

theorem exists_bijective_stage_of_filtered_pushouts
    {J : Type v} [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] [UnivLE.{v, u}]
    (D E : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (α : D ⟶ E)
    (cD : Cocone D) (cE : Cocone E) (hD : IsColimit cD) (hE : IsColimit cE)
    (f : cD.pt ⟶ cE.pt)
    (hf : ∀ j, α.app j ≫ cE.ι.app j = cD.ι.app j ≫ f)
    (hbij : Function.Bijective f)
    (hfp : ∀ j, (α.app j).hom.FinitePresentation)
    (hpush : ∀ {j k} (r : j ⟶ k), IsPushout (α.app j) (D.map r)
      (E.map r) (α.app k)) :
    ∃ j, Function.Bijective (α.app j)
